message:
fix(ka-pc r7): the X pair's ups are releases in the one shared rule; a write the fence refused before any byte is a cancellation, not a failure (Codex N1, N2)

- N1 the shared core's release rule (release_identity, now also control_input_release_identity) counts the X1 / X2
  mouse ups (VK 5 / 6) with left / right / middle; the gate asks that one rule (no copy). So an X up queued before
  the fence survives DropAllButReleases, and the ups the fence makes (enqueue_release_for_pressed_mouse_buttons) are
  taken by the drain; the viewer's own capability fence still keeps every X edge away from a host that did not
  advertise the pair
- N2 the gated link records why a write was refused -- by the fence before any byte of the message, in the middle of a
  message, by the test hook; every caller of a failed exchange takes that one reason (gate_take_failure): only
  'not started' is a cancellation (InputOutcome::Cancelled, the drain goes on); a cut message, a refused release and
  a transport failure stay failures (no resume after the fence: the loop ends). The verdict counts acks, logon-gate
  skips and fence cancellations apart, and the log says each (an InputAck is no longer claimed for what was not sent)
- ka_pc_fence_test: N1 -- with the r7 line removed from the shared rule (a mutant) FAIL 3 (an X up dropped, the drain
  takes none; and the verdict is Confirmed with them missing), r7 PASS, and no X edge to a host without the pair;
  N2 -- r6's mapping closes the fence as Failed with the held Ctrl's up still queued, r7 waits, sends it, Confirmed
  with 1 ack + 1 cancelled; a cut message / hook refusal / no-ack release are failures
- shell e2e: the fence's log line is 'releases confirmed after N ms -- ... acknowledged by the host ...'
